display.title: Sefiras HaOmer: Counting Days and the Lost Dime
display.summary_short: Why we count the days of the Omer: every day is a precious gift from Hashem, and a little girl's lost dime teaches us not to waste the time we have now.
display.summary_long: A short talk from the Tzivos Hashem radio show, given in the middle of Sefiras HaOmer. Uncle Yossi points out that during Sefirah all we do is count days, and we even say a brachah on it, because each day is precious and each new number reminds us that today must be better than yesterday. Time cannot be bought, stopped or brought back. He tells of Miriam, who loses a dime and keeps crying even after her mother gives her new ones, because she would have had more if not for the lost one. Her mother explains that she must forget the lost dime and take care not to lose the ones she has now. So too, time is a gift from Hashem; like a person counting precious jewels, we should fill every moment with Torah and mitzvos, and Hashem will lengthen our days, as we say in the Shema.
display.lesson: Time is a precious gift from Hashem: don't waste it, and make each day better than the one before.
